chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a slave girl freed by my brother, who used to serve with the other slave girls and was part of his household. He bequeathed to me to spend upon her from the middle (of the legacy). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If she was with the slave girls and was supervising over them, then spend upon her, and follow his bequest.'

key_terms.مُحَرَّرَةٍ: A female slave who has been freed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a freed slave woman who continues to live in the household after her master's death?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial rights of a freed slave woman who remains in the master's household, emphasizing that her maintenance should be drawn from the estate's middle portion (al-wasat) as per the deceased's will. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle that emancipation does not sever the bond of financial responsibility if the woman continues to reside with the family, ensuring her dignity and stability are preserved through the heir's adherence to the specific bequest.
